I have decided that I dont like the second post for Dear Leader so i'm doing this again from the top.

[spoiler=
[b]Dear Leader[/b]
Act 2: I don't like suits.]
[i]Marcus Vanderbilt holds a deep contempt for what he sees as the ridiculous and pompous standards of Westmorian high society. In a way, he is much like President Holt - a maverick with no regard for the rules, who doesn't care for what others think of him. As part of his wanton disregard for the cultural norms of being a politician, he makes it a point every day to come to Parliament sessions dressed in casual clothes. Many of his colleagues despise his aversion of prim and proper suits, but as said before, he couldn't care any less. [/i]

...

[i]"I know you don't like suits, Marcus, but did you really have to arrive in THAT on the most important day of your life?"[/i]

Marcus stares at Joel dead in the eyes. "Yes. I don't like suits. Suits are ridiculous and uncomfortable, and I'm not going to subject myself to them so I can uphold the equally ridiculous standards the culture wants to impose on me. I am a free man in a free country, Joel, you can't force me to do something I don't like."

"Well, in some cultures like ours, it's considered disrespectful to come to a formal event in a shirt that says 'F*ck the Police.'  I will let you know, Marcus, that the Commissioner of the Federal Police will be in attendance today, and I think it would be unwise to offend him given the work he does for you."

"Unless Commissioner Kern is secretly Abe Saffron in disguise, I don't care what he thinks of me or what he'll do to me. I am going to be the next President whether he likes it or not. I am quite literally untouchable, remember that."

Joel puts his hand on Marcus's shoulder. "Fine. Don't wear a suit. But at least wear a jacket or something. It's cold outside."

"Whatever." Marcus brushes Joel's hand off of him and walks to his office.

[i]Thud.[/i]

Inside the office, Marcus reaches inside the pocket of his pants and produces a small orange bottle. On the bottle, it reads in large black letters "VICODIN". He pops the cap off with his thumb and gulps down three of the little white pills inside.

Many people know that he struggles with a bum leg, hence his limping. Multiple times, he has refused to use a cane to make it easier for him to move; he believes that a cane makes him look stupid.

What most don't know is that because of his crippled right leg, he takes a copious amount of pain medication, and as a result has a crippling addiction to hydrocodone, known better as Vicodin. Every hour of every day, it hurts like hell, and on some days the pain is so blisteringly bad that he can't bring himself to get out of bed. He is plainly aware that he is addicted to Vicodin, yet he doesn't care.

The pain saps the life out of him.

The drugs give that life back to him.

Marcus grabs a coat from his office and walks to the front steps of Parliament House. He hastily stuffs the vicodin back into his pants as he makes his way to the front doors of the building.

...

[i]"Good morning, people of New Westmore."[/i]

Marcus stands at the top of the stairs to Parliament House as he delivers his inaugural speech to a mass of reporters and journalists. Nearby, a selection of government officials stand and observe him silently.

"Today, I stand before you not as the second-in-command, but as the leader of this fine nation. In the wake of President Holt's untimely death, I have been..."

[i]Good god.[/i] He thinks to himself. [i]This speech is just so boring. Do they actually want me to read this?[/i]

"You know what, I'm not going to read this bog standard political drivel. I've foisted into this position by my colleagues against my own will, and now I shall serve as your President for the remainder of what should have been Holt's term."

Some of the reporters raise eyebrows. Joel shoots him a cold stare. Marcus ignores it and continues talking.

"Admittedly, in the last three weeks or so, I have not been caught up with international happenings. Not a good start for me, seeing as I am in a position of high power over this nation. What I do know is that I do not care for the rising tensions between THEP and EDU. It is not a fight we should be getting involved in at all."

A reporter shouts a question out at him. "Don't we have obligations to THEP? How about the Westmorians caught in the warzone? What are you going to do about that?"

Marcus continues talking. By this point, he is no longer talking on behalf of the government; his thoughts unabated flow out to the masses. "I do not intend on sending our men to fight this pointless war, nor do I want to entertain the nuclear folly on display there. If there are Westmorians stuck in Nestor-Sikirsk, we will send repatriation flights - why am I explaining this part? This much is obvious, is it not?"

Joel presses his fingers to the bridge of his nose. The government officials now look visibly uncomfortable.

"Right. Now onto domestic matters. This speech wanted me to say I wouldn't change the status quo in regards to the projects and policies he has already greenlighted, so I won't. I'm happy with how it is, I'm happy with what Holt has already kicked off and it is my full intention to see to it that his initiatives are complete by the time this term ends."

"Anyway, that's all for now, I guess. Question time, anyone?"

The reporters hurl question after question about his stance on the Nestor-Sikirsk War. Every response he gives seems to upset the reporters more and more, and visibly upsets his Parliament colleagues.

[i]"So you really don't care about THEP?"[/i]
"No, I don't, if anything I think they have overstepped their boundaries with the nukes they have introduced into this conflict."

[i]"Are you in support of the EDU?"[/i]
"No comment."

[i]"Do you intend to pull out of THEP for good?"[/i]
"Possibly. Again, no intention humouring their actions."

[i]How are you going to send repatriation flights...

Are you going to drive us into reclusion...[/i]

Joel finally snaps and storms up to Marcus.

"I'm sorry everyone, question time is now over, Mr. President is making some incredibly brash calls we [i]DID NOT[/i] agree on. Please don't take anything he says here as official until we say so." He grabs Marcus by the shoulder and drags him behind the doors of Parliament House.

...

[i]"Marcus, what the hell was that?"[/i]

"I gave my speech, I gave my thoughts."

"Why would you try to anger our allies in THEP? Are you out of your mind?"

"No, I'm not. I'm of sound mind, Joel."

"Well clearly you're not- look, we'll handle the situation from here, but PLEASE don't be so brash going forward, Marcus!"

"Fine, fine, I won't."

"OK I have to know: were you acting like that because your pain?"

"No. No, I wasn't."

"Right. Be honest."

"Yes. And because I don't like THEP. It's that simple, Joel!"

"Well, if you don't like THEP, use the systems we have in place to express that dislike. Don't go off the rails like that!"

"Fine, I won't."

"Good. You better hope to God nothing comes of this, man."
[/spoiler]
